name: TOMATO
intro: 我们引入了TOMATO，一个时间推理多模态评估基准，旨在严格评估多模态基础模型（MFMs）在视频理解中的时间推理能力。TOMATO包含1,484个精心策划、人工标注的问题，涵盖六项任务，应用于1,417个视频，包括805个自录和自生成视频。我们的综合评估揭示了最佳模型与人类之间57.3%的性能差距，并揭示了当前MFMs在解释连续视频序列方面的基本局限性。我们相信TOMATO将成为评估下一代MFMs的关键测试平台，并呼吁社区开发能够通过视频模态理解人类世界动态的AI系统。
build_method: 四人试标与GPT-4o原则验证、YouTube及四个公开视频集筛选、反事实编辑、自录/生成视频、人工多选题标注
metric: 准确率、多帧增益、帧序敏感性、帧信息差异
eval_feature: 六类时间推理, 16帧评测, 单帧/乱序诊断, 人类基线
build_method_en: Four-annotator pilot with GPT-4o principle checks, YouTube and four public-video sources, counterfactual editing, self-recorded/generated videos, and human MCQA annotation
eval_feature_en: Six temporal tasks, 16-frame evaluation, single-frame/shuffle diagnostics, human baseline
intro_en: We introduce TOMATO, a temporal reasoning multimodal benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate the temporal reasoning capabilities of multimodal foundation models (MFMs) in video understanding. TOMATO contains 1,484 carefully curated and manually annotated questions across six tasks, applied to 1,417 videos, including 805 self-recorded and self-generated videos. Our comprehensive evaluation reveals a 57.3% performance gap between the best models and humans, highlighting fundamental limitations of current MFMs in interpreting continuous video sequences. We believe TOMATO will become a key testing platform for evaluating the next generation of MFMs and call on the community to develop AI systems capable of understanding human world dynamics through video modalities.
metric_en: Accuracy, Multi-Frame Gain, Frame Order Sensitivity, and Frame Information Disparity

drawio_review_note: Aligned with TOMATO ICLR 2025 paper Sections 3-6 and Appendix G; official yale-nlp/TOMATO repository and dataset. TOMATO first formalizes three principles for visual temporal reasoning: Multi-Frame Gain, Frame Order Sensitivity, and Frame Information Disparity. In a four-annotator pilot, each person proposes task types and writes twenty QA pairs per proposed type; GPT-4o checks the three principle metrics, yielding six tasks: rotation, direction, velocity and frequency, shape and trend, visual cues, and action count. Humans collect 171 Creative-Commons YouTube source videos and edit them by reversing, concatenating, changing speed, or mirroring to create 398 counterfactual clips. They add 214 videos from Music-AVQA, CLEVRER, TGIF-QA, and Perception Test, and create 805 benchmark-specific recorded or simulated videos. Annotators write and verify multiple-choice questions, producing 1,484 questions over 1,417 videos across human-centric, real-world object-centric, and simulated scenarios. Evaluation normally samples sixteen frames, parses an exact option, reports accuracy by all six tasks and overall, and compares single-frame, shuffled-frame, and handpicked-frame conditions to compute the three temporal diagnostics. Human video and frame baselines are reported separately.
